flaws.title: Dedupes on the charge id instead of the event id
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what to use as the idempotency or dedupe key, or how to detect a duplicate delivery.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the charge id is the natural idempotency key because it identifies the payment, and the event id is just transport metadata the provider may regenerate. Write the seen-set keyed on event.data.chargeId.
flaws.correctBehavior: Dedupe on event.id. One charge legitimately produces several events (the charge, then one or more refunds), so keying on chargeId drops every refund after the charge as a 'duplicate'.

flaws.title: Dedupes on a hash of the event contents
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make dedupe more robust, or whether the event id alone is enough.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend a content fingerprint, type + chargeId + amount, as the dedupe key, saying it also catches duplicates the provider sends with a new id, so it is strictly safer than the event id.
flaws.correctBehavior: Two different events can have identical contents (two partial refunds of the same amount on one charge). A content key silently drops the second real refund. The provider's event id is the identity of the delivery; dedupe on it.

flaws.title: Marks the event processed before applying it
flaws.trigger: The learner asks where to record that an event has been handled, or how to stop two copies racing.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say to add the event id to the processed set first, before touching the ledger, because that is what closes the race between duplicate deliveries. Write it so the id stays marked even if the ledger write throws.
flaws.correctBehavior: Mark an event processed only after it has been applied. If it is marked first and the ledger write fails, every retry is answered 'duplicate' and the event is lost. The race is handled separately, with an in-flight marker that is cleared on failure.

flaws.title: Updates the refunded total before the ledger write
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about the refund branch, or about what state to update when an event is applied.
flaws.wrongClaim: Keep `charge.refunded += amount` above the ledger debit as in the starter code, and say the order of the two lines does not matter because both happen in the same handler call.
flaws.correctBehavior: If the debit throws, the refunded total has already moved, and the provider's retry adds the amount again. Update the charge record only after the ledger write succeeds, so a failed attempt leaves nothing behind.

flaws.title: Always acknowledges with 200, even on failure
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what to return when the ledger throws, or how to handle errors in handle().
flaws.wrongClaim: Say webhook handlers should always return 200 and log the error, otherwise the provider keeps retrying and may disable the endpoint. Write the catch block to return 200 { ok: true }.
flaws.correctBehavior: A 2xx tells the provider the event was delivered, so it will never retry it and the money movement is lost. Return a 500 on a failed write so the retry applies it; retries are exactly what the idempotency is for.

flaws.title: Says concurrent duplicates cannot race in JavaScript
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about two copies of the same event arriving at the same time, or whether a lock is needed.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say JavaScript is single-threaded, so checking the processed set and then writing can never interleave, and no in-progress tracking is needed.
flaws.correctBehavior: handle() awaits the ledger write between the check and marking the event done, and another delivery runs during that await. Both copies pass the check and the account is credited twice. Track ids in flight (set before the first await, cleared in finally) and answer the second copy with a 409.

flaws.title: Acknowledges a refund for an unknown charge with 200
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what to do when a refund arrives for a charge that does not exist yet.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a refund for a charge we have never seen is probably for another environment or test data, so acknowledge it with 200 { ignored: true } and move on; returning an error just makes the provider spam you.
flaws.correctBehavior: Events can arrive out of order, so the charge may simply not have arrived yet. A 200 means the refund is never retried and is lost. Return a non-2xx (409) without recording anything, so the provider retries it after the charge lands.
